subject: Modelling continuous covariates using RW2 latent model

messages.author: 6b8a5a035983f03e
messages.subject: Modelling continuous covariates using RW2 latent model
parts:
I am looking to model a couple of continuous covariates using a second order random walk (RW2) latent model that allows for possible non-linear relationships.

When I tried to use the code f(tmean, model = "rw2"), I received the error message that the locations were too close: min(diff(sort(x)))/diff(range(x)) = 3.319e-09 < 1e-03 and that I could fix this with some kind of binning and to see ?inla.group.

I found the code on how to use inla.group to reduce the number of unique values, and will try  it. However, when I was looking through the online book, "Bayesian Inference with INLA" by Virgilio Gómez-Rubio, it said that RW2 could be used to model continuous variables by using the "values" argument. "In particular, the values of the covariate can be binned so that they are associated with a particular value of the vector of random effects." 

What is the values argument, and is it different than using inla.group? If it is different, how do you incorporate the values argument into code for the RW2 latent model where you are modelling a non-linear relationship? 

Thanks,

Kristin

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Modelling continuous covariates using RW2 latent model
parts:
values are where the f() model is defined. by default it is taken as
'x', in f(x,...), but this is not always correct.

to close values, as you mention below, is to avoid numerical singular
matrices, which otherwise may arise [which then signal an error and even
more confusion...].

yes, either you have to fix those manually, or 'inla.group' is an
automated alternative.

H
